subject: Budget range validation - PayBridge procurement thresholds
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@paybridge.com>, Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@paybridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: quick recap + pricing estimates (tokens & monthly bands)

Hi Samantha / Alex —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and the next items I said I'd follow up on:

What I heard you use-case-wise:
- Real-time customer support generation and post-payment reconciliation (latency sensitive; majority of calls are ~3–5 prompt+response turns).
- Expected growth from pilot -> prod in Q4.
- Security: SOC2 + data residency for production (we discussed Dedicated/Private options).

Ask / next steps from my side:
1) A rough monthly spend band that gets you through procurement (so we can propose the right quote structure).
2) Any procurement thresholds (PO size / contracts desk) or preferred term length that would change pricing.

I'll send an example of token-volume to $/1M tokens unit-econ scenarios and a simple monthly spend band matrix so you can validate internally. Attaching the latest pricing sheet and a one-page procurement checklist for your legal/procurement team.

Attachments: redwood_pricing_v2.pdf, procurement_checklist.xlsx

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call with procurement if helpful.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
https://redwood.com

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@paybridge.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@paybridge.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: quick recap + pricing estimates (tokens & monthly bands)

Thanks Dylan — good recap. A couple quick clarifying Qs so we can figure out procurement routing:

- For procurement: our threshold for a full procurement review is typically any multi-month commitment or quote > $50,000. Anything above that we need Procurement + Legal review (two-week target for standard SOW/PO).
- For IT/Security: SOC2 evidence is required for prod; we'll validate the docs but that part looks fine from today's demo.

For the budget band, the exec sponsor wants to see 3 scenarios (pilot / scale / enterprise) with expected monthly spend and a per-1M token estimate. Can you include an estimate for both hosted (pay-as-you-go) and reserved (discounted commit) options?

Also: who should procurement expect to receive the contract/quote from? Email or DocuSign?

Appreciate it — if you can send that today we'll try to get internal alignment and let you know whether we need a procurement kickoff.

Best,
Samantha Lee
Head of Procurement | PayBridge
Samantha.Lee@paybridge.com

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@paybridge.com>, Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@paybridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: quick recap + pricing estimates (tokens & monthly bands)

Hi Samantha / Alex —

Thanks — below are three simple scenarios (tokens = total tokens in/out per month) with unit economics expressed as $ per 1M tokens. Numbers are illustrative and assume a mix of generation + embeddings workload; final pricing depends on model family, latency SLO, and whether you choose hosted vs Dedicated reserved capacity.

Scenarios (hosted PAYG / example list price):
- Pilot (low traffic): 5M tokens/month => unit-rate: $600 per 1M tokens => estimated monthly bill: $3,000
- Scale (growing): 50M tokens/month => unit-rate: $600 per 1M tokens => estimated monthly bill: $30,000
- Enterprise (high throughput): 250M tokens/month => list unit-rate: $600 per 1M tokens => estimated monthly bill: $150,000

Reserved / Dedicated commits (examples of committed-discount levels):
- Small commit (>= $25k/mo): ~10% discount => example $540 per 1M tokens
- Mid commit (>= $100k/mo): ~20% discount => example $480 per 1M tokens
- Large commit (>= $200k/mo): ~25%+ discount => example $450 per 1M tokens (or lower with multi-year)

Notes on procurement thresholds and recommendations:
- Given PayBridge's stated procurement review threshold of $50k, the Scale example (50M tokens => $30k/mo PAYG) is below that in month 1, but if you plan to commit up-front or expect multi-month billing it may cross the threshold.
- If procurement needs a vendor quote >$50k for a purchase order, we can structure a 3-month or annual invoice to align with your PO workflows.
- We can also provide a formal quote/DocuSign SOW that procurement can use; procurement should expect the quote from redwood-contracts@redwood.com (we'll route through Marissa on the account).

Attached: redwood_pricing_v2.pdf (detailed rates by model family), procurement_checklist.xlsx

Example next steps:
1) Confirm which scenario (Pilot / Scale / Enterprise) is closest to your expected first 90 days.
2) Confirm procurement review threshold & preferred quote flow (email vs DocuSign + PO terms).
3) If helpful, schedule a short procurement kickoff — Marissa (cc) can own the quote and legal/contract routing.

Happy to jump on a 15-minute call to walk procurement through the pricing sheet.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0192

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Jul 2026 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: support for PayBridge procurement / pricing flexibility

Dylan — quick internal note so we have alignment before we ship the official quote to Samantha.

- I'm happy to own the quote and routing to procurement (redwood-contracts@redwood.com).
- We can offer an aggressive commit-based price for PayBridge if they can commit to >= $200k/mo or annualized equivalent: target ~$450 per 1M tokens (or special negotiated unit econ depending on model selection).
- For pilots under $50k total we should stick to standard PAYG list pricing to avoid adding complexity.
- I'll prepare a one-page tradeoff table (commit vs PAYG) and a DocuSign-ready SOW template for procurement to review.

I'll aim to have the formal quote and SOW ready by EOD tomorrow if Dylan confirms the scenario they want to pursue.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
